title: Region-aware RBAC blueprint and compact roleset model
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and deliver a compact, region-aware RBAC roleset and enforcement model for RBAC v2. This ticket defines a resource hierarchy that includes global, organization, region, and zone levels; a minimal canonical roleset (viewer/operator/admin/allocator) with scope bindings; an explicit deny and temporal elevation mechanism; standardized audit tagging; and SSO/SAML attribute mappings to support enterprise provisioning. Goal: produce a design doc, reference permission matrix, enforcement contract for the API gateway and runtime authorization hooks, and a migration path from RBAC v1 with a compatibility shim for existing service principals.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by Security and Platform leads
Permission matrix (CSV) that maps canonical roles to actions and resources across all hierarchy levels
Policy evaluation order defined (explicit deny, resource scoped allow, inherited allow) and validated with unit tests
SSO/SAML mapping spec with example attribute->role mappings for Okta and Azure AD
Audit schema defined (fields + sample events) and integrated into logging pipeline prototype
Migration plan with automated mapping script and a rollback strategy documented
tasks: Finalize resource hierarchy and canonical scope identifiers (glob, org, region, zone, resource-id)
Draft compact roleset and permission aliases for common actions (read/write/manage, allocate)
Define explicit deny semantics and temporal elevation token format
Create acceptance tests for policy evaluator and ordering
Write SAML attribute mapping examples and provisioning flow for Okta/Azure AD
Schema audit events and add telemetry tags to auth decisions
Prototype gateway enforcement hook and runtime SDK check integration
Author migration CLI to map RBAC v1 roles to v2 canonical roles with manual overrides
audit_considerations: Every authorization decision must emit: actor_id, principal_type, evaluated_policy_id, resource_scope, decision (allow/deny), reason_code, request_id, timestamp
Include region and zone tags on every event for downstream billing/forensics
Audit events must be immutable and append-only; write schema for long-term storage and retention
Sensitive fields (user_email, token) must be redacted before external forwarding
Attach trace_id to link auth event with serving runtime spans
sso_saml_mapping: Recommended source_of_truth: group membership + SAML roles attribute. Prefer group names like 'redwood:ops:us-west' over opaque role ids
Map SAML attribute 'roles' -> canonical role set using a translation table; example: 'prod-admin' -> 'allocator/admin', 'read-only' -> 'viewer'
Support multi-valued attributes and precedence rules (explicit role attribute beat group-derived roles)
Provide SCIM-based provisioning guidance to sync org/region membership into our internal directory
Edge case: service principals without SAML must be provisioned via service tokens with a required 'provisioning_ticket' workflow
migration_plan: Create a discovery job to enumerate current RBAC v1 bindings across tenants and services
Generate a proposed mapping file using heuristics + confidence scores; surface low-confidence bindings for manual review
Rollout in three phases: audit-only (emit v2 decision simulation), opt-in enforcement per org, global cutover with fallback window
Provide admin rollback endpoints and automated remediation for accidental lockouts
Post-cutover audit runbook and customer communication templates
decisions: Use a compact canonical roleset (viewer/operator/admin/allocator) to simplify UI and reduce policy explosion
Policy evaluation order: explicit deny -> exact-scope allow -> inherited allow -> global default deny
Enforcement surface: gateway for coarse-grained route-level checks, runtime SDK for fine-grained resource checks (both emit same audit schema)
Temporal elevation implemented as short-lived elevation tokens issued by Admin Console with justification and expiry
SSO mapping will prefer deterministic translation tables over free-text parsing to avoid mapping drift
open_questions: Do we need permission-level interpolation for third-party plugins (e.g., allow 'cache:flush' without granting 'service:manage')?
How should we represent cross-region resource ownership (single owner vs. replicated ownership)?
What SLA do we commit for provisioning latency when using SCIM group sync during onboarding?
Is 'allocator' role scoped to dedicated capacity pools or general resource allocation? Clarify with infra team
